title: Accessing Olfactory Habituation in Drosophila melanogaster with a T-maze Paradigm
author: Ourania Semelidou
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML
materials: Materials and Reagents 14 ml Falcon tubes Glass vials for odorants (diameter: 2.2 cm, height: 9.5 cm) Drosophila melanogaster 3-Octanol (CAS number: 589-98-0; ACROS Organics, catalog number: AC203770500), store at RT Benzaldehyde (CAS number: 100-52-7; Sigma, catalog number: 418099), store at 4 °C Ethyl acetate (CAS number: 141-78-6; Sigma, catalog number: 34858), store at RT Butanedione (CAS number: 431-03-8; Sigma, catalog number: B85307 ), store at RT Brewers Yeast (CAS number: 68876-77-7; ACROS Organics, catalog number: AC368080010), store at 4 °C Drosophila food (see Recipes) Semolina Whole wheat flour Brown sugar Fructose Soy flour CaCl 2 Dry yeast Nipagen Propionic acid

Recipes Drosophila food 140 g semolina 180 g whole wheat flour 180 g brown sugar 72 g fructose 15 g soy flour 6 g CaCl 2 210 g dry yeast 150 ml Nipagen (10% in EtOH) 25 ml Propionic acid Bring up to 8.5 L final volume with house distilled water

steps.title: Assemble T‑maze apparatus
steps.instruction: Attach the side panels and the elevator to the base using the aluminum screws; when all four screws are in place tighten them crosswise until snug but not forced to avoid damaging the plexiglass threads. Attach the vacuum adaptors to the vacuum ports and verify that the elevator moves up and down freely while remaining snug.

steps.title: Prepare Drosophila food
steps.instruction: Mix 140 g semolina, 180 g whole‑wheat flour, 180 g brown sugar, 72 g fructose, 15 g soy flour, 6 g CaCl₂, 210 g dry yeast, 150 ml Nipagen (10 % in EtOH) and 25 ml propionic acid. Bring the mixture to a final volume of 8.5 L with house‑distilled water.

steps.title: Generate Cantonised w1118 background
steps.instruction: Backcross control flies carrying the w1118 mutation to Canton‑S for at least 10 generations to obtain Cantonised‑w1118. Then outcross all experimental Drosophila lines with Cantonised‑w1118 for six generations to equalise the genetic background.

steps.title: Rear flies under experimental conditions
steps.instruction: Raise flies on the standard wheat‑flour‑sugar food supplemented with soy flour and CaCl₂ under a 14:10 h light‑dark cycle, 60 % relative humidity, at 25 °C (or at 18 °C until hatching when using the TARGET system). For Gal4 lines keep flies at 30 °C overnight to enhance transgene expression. For TARGET‑system experiments keep flies at 30 °C for 2–3 days prior to testing. For neuronal silencing with Shibire^ts place flies at 32–33 °C for 30 min before the experiment. For neuronal activation with TRPA1 transfer flies to 30–31 °C for the desired activation period.

steps.title: Anesthetize and group flies
steps.instruction: Anesthetize flies with CO₂ at least one day before the experiment and separate them into groups of 50–60 individuals. Place each group in a food vial at the temperature appropriate for their genotype (25 °C for controls, 30 °C for Gal4 lines, 32–33 °C for Shibire^ts, etc.) under the same 14:10 h light‑dark and 60 % humidity conditions.

steps.title: Pre‑experiment fly handling
steps.instruction: Transfer flies to fresh food vials approximately 1 h before the experiment, keep the vials in a dark box at the temperature they were previously kept. For Shibire^ts experiments use pre‑warmed vials kept at 32–33 °C and transfer the groups sequentially so that all experience exactly 30 min at that temperature before testing.

steps.title: Prepare behavior room and clean T‑maze
steps.instruction: Clean the T‑maze and all arms with a soft cloth. Verify that arms fit tightly and that the airflow is stable at 500 ppm (0.5 ml/min). If this is the first use, run a control trial without odor to confirm no side bias. Set room humidity to 60–70 % and temperature to 23–24 °C. Perform all experiments under dim red light.

steps.title: Prepare odor solutions and prime system
steps.instruction: Store reagents as follows: 3‑Octanol (CAS 589‑98‑0, ACROS Organics, cat AC203770500) at room temperature (RT); Benzaldehyde (CAS 100‑52‑7, Sigma, cat 418099) at 4 °C; Ethyl acetate (CAS 141‑78‑6, Sigma, cat 34858) at RT; 2,3‑Butanedione (CAS 431‑03‑8, Sigma, cat B85307) at RT. Prepare odor sources: • 3‑Octanol – add 1 ml of pure 3‑Octanol to a glass vial (diameter 2.2 cm, height 9.5 cm). • Benzaldehyde – add 100 µl of pure Benzaldehyde to a 14 ml Falcon tube. • Ethyl acetate – add 10 µl of a 0.1 % (v/v) dilution in water to a 14 ml Falcon tube. • 2,3‑Butanedione – add 10 µl of a 0.5 % (v/v) dilution in water to a 14 ml Falcon tube. Dilute other odorants either in water (ethyl acetate, 2,3‑butanedione) or in isopropyl myristate (Octanol, Benzaldehyde). Connect the odor source to the T‑maze and let odor flow for 30 min to prime the system.

steps.title: Perform odor avoidance/attraction test
steps.instruction: Clamp the T‑maze together tightly. Load the flies into a clean arm and attach it to the upper part of the maze. Slide the elevator so the receptacle aligns with the arm, tap gently to transfer flies into the receptacle and slide the elevator down quickly to trap them. Connect air tubing to one side, odor tubing to the opposite side, and attach the vacuum. Slide the elevator down and allow the flies to choose for 90 s for aversive odors or 180 s for attractive odors while maintaining airflow at 500 ppm. Move the elevator up to trap flies in the two arms, then transfer the contents of each arm into separate numbered tubes. Clean the elevator receptacle, re‑attach the arms and repeat for all repetitions. After the experiment transfer the collection rack to –80 °C, wait ~15 min, then count flies and record the numbers in the air‑arm and odor‑arm together with genotype.

steps.title: Habituation training and testing
steps.instruction: Load flies into a dedicated training arm and attach it to the upper part of the maze; use a different arm for each odor if multiple odors are tested. Slide the elevator so flies are trapped in the arm while odor can flow. Connect vacuum tubing first, then odor tubing, and set odor flow to 500 ppm. Expose flies to odor for the designated period: 1 min for latency experiments, 4 min or 30 min for habituation experiments. For pulse protocols replace the continuous exposure with: – 1 min → 2 × 30 s pulses with 8 s inter‑stimulus interval (ISI); – 4 min → 4 × 1 min pulses with 15 s ISI; – 30 min → 3 × 10 min pulses with 2.5 min ISI. Disconnect the odor tubing while keeping the vacuum on for air flow, wait 30 s, slide the elevator to align the receptacle with the training arm, tap gently to transfer flies into the receptacle and slide the elevator down quickly to trap them. Continue with the odor avoidance/attraction test described in the previous step.

steps.title: Dishabituation with electric shock
steps.instruction: Set the Grass Stimulator to a 1.2 s pulse at 45 V. Load flies into an arm equipped with a custom copper grid and attach it to the upper part of the maze. Train flies with the chosen odor exposure (1, 4 or 30 min) as in the habituation step while the copper grid is connected to the stimulus wires via crocodile clips. At the end of the exposure disconnect the odor tubing and immediately deliver a single 45 V shock. Remove the crocodile clips, keep the vacuum on for 30 s (air flow), then slide the elevator to align the receptacle with the copper‑grid arm, tap to transfer flies into the receptacle and slide the elevator down quickly. Proceed to the odor avoidance/attraction test.

steps.title: Dishabituation with vortex
steps.instruction: Train flies with the chosen odor exposure as above. After the exposure disconnect the odor tubing and remove the arm from the maze, sealing the open end with your hand. Vortex the sealed arm for 3 s at maximum speed. Re‑attach the arm to the maze, connect the vacuum tubing (air flow), wait 30 s, slide the elevator to align the receptacle with the training arm, tap to transfer flies into the receptacle and slide the elevator down quickly. Continue with the odor avoidance/attraction test.

steps.title: Dishabituation with yeast puff
steps.instruction: Prepare a 30 % (w/v) yeast solution in water and set up a dedicated arm and tubing for this odor, ensuring odor flow of 500 ppm. Train flies with the chosen odor exposure as above. After exposure disconnect the odor tubing and remove the arm, sealing it with your hand. Transfer the flies to the yeast‑puff arm, connect the yeast‑puff tubing and deliver odor for 3 s, then remove the tubing and keep the vacuum on for air flow. Wait 30 s, slide the elevator to align the receptacle with the training arm, tap to transfer flies into the receptacle and slide the elevator down quickly. Proceed to the odor avoidance/attraction test.

steps.title: Spontaneous recovery assay
steps.instruction: Follow the habituation training and testing procedure. After the fifth step of the testing phase (Step D5) transfer the flies to fresh food vials for 6 min, then continue with the sixth step of the testing phase (Step D6) which is the standard odor avoidance/attraction assessment.
